issues.legal_issue: A lessee under a mining lease is not entitled to enforce a future renewal covenant against the State after the estate vests free from encumbrances.
material_facts: The lessee held a fifteen-year lease of mineral-bearing land that included an option to renew at the lessee’s choice.
During the lease term, the estate vested in the State free from encumbrances and from the interests of the lessors and lessees.
The lessee remained in possession for the balance of the original term under a statutory lease deemed granted by the State.
The lessee sought specific performance of the original lease’s renewal covenant.
issues.conclusion: The renewal covenant did not bind the State after vesting, and the lessee was not entitled to specific performance of it.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 3, 4(a), and 10 of the Bihar Land Reforms Act, 1950, vesting extinguishes encumbrances, while a subsisting mining lease is replaced by a statutory lease for the remainder of its term on terms and conditions mutatis mutandis equivalent to those of the original lease. A future renewal covenant is a covenant running with the land, creates no present interest in land, and is an encumbrance extinguished on vesting. The court approved the reasoning in The State of Bihar v. Indian Copper Corporation Ltd., I.L.R. 38 Pat. 1160.

rule.if: claim_to_enforce_future_lease_renewal and subsisting_mining_lease and estate_vested_free_of_encumbrances and renewal_option_is_future_covenant and statutory_lease_covers_only_remaining_original_term

predicates.claim_to_enforce_future_lease_renewal: A lessee seeks to enforce a promise that a lease will be renewed in the future.
predicates.subsisting_mining_lease: A mining lease is in force when the estate containing the leased land vests.
predicates.estate_vested_free_of_encumbrances: The estate vests in the State without encumbrances or the former owners’ and lessees’ interests.
predicates.renewal_option_is_future_covenant: The lease gives the lessee an option to obtain a later lease, rather than presently granting an interest for that later term.
predicates.statutory_lease_covers_only_remaining_or: By operation of law, the State grants the lessee a lease only for the unexpired remainder of the original lease term.

issues.definition: When a lessee seeks to enforce a future renewal promise in a subsisting mining lease, and the estate vests free of encumbrances while only the remaining original term continues by statutory lease, the future renewal promise cannot be enforced against the State.

issues.legal_issue: A mining-concession renewal rule for government grants does not entitle a holder of a statutory mining lease to renewal.
material_facts: Following vesting, the lessee held a statutory lease for the remainder of the original lease term.
The lessee relied on a mining-concession rule providing for renewal of mining leases at the lessee’s option.

The court found that the rule applied to grants made by government, not leases arising by statute; it also observed that, even if the rule applied, the relevant statutory lease period had expired long before the appeal.
issues.conclusion: The mining-concession rule did not give the lessee a right to renewal of the statutory lease; in any event, the relevant period for a claimed renewal had already expired.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 40 of the Mineral Concession Rules, 1949 applies to mining leases granted by government and not to statutory leases arising under section 10 of the Bihar Land Reforms Act, 1950. The court further stated that, even assuming the rule applied, the duration of the original lease for this purpose could be no longer than the period from vesting until expiry of the original lease, and the period for which renewal could have been claimed had elapsed.

predicates.claim_to_renew_mining_lease: A leaseholder seeks renewal of a mining lease.
predicates.lease_created_by_statutory_operation: The lease arose by operation of legislation rather than by a government grant.
predicates.renewal_claim_relies_on_general_mining_c: The leaseholder relies on a general rule governing renewal of mining leases.

issues.definition: When a leaseholder seeks renewal of a mining lease created by legislation and relies on a general mining-concession renewal rule, that rule does not entitle the holder to renew the statutory lease.
